name: Ronald Reagan
role: US president (1981-1989); governor of California (1967-1975); film and television actor
summary: Reagan was a movement conservative who held that government was the main obstacle to prosperity and liberty. He cut taxes and regulation, favored free trade and school choice, opposed abortion, backed school prayer and a large military, and sought to defeat Soviet communism through pressure while also negotiating arms reductions. He signed an immigration law that combined enforcement with legalization for long-resident unauthorized immigrants.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In 1964 he attacked compulsory government medical programs for the elderly, citing France's bankrupt Medicare scheme, and later sought to slow Medicare and Medicaid growth rather than extend state coverage.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Declared in 1981 that government was the problem, not the solution, and built his program on freeing enterprise from government rules; in 1989 said liberty contracts as government expands.

public-ownership.rationale: Sent legislation to return Conrail to the private sector 'where it belongs' and warned in 1964 that government planners were hollowing out ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Signed the 1981 across-the-board cut and the 1986 act that cut top rates sharply, and pledged to oppose any attempt to raise tax rates; he did sign smaller tax increases such as TEFRA in 1982.

unions-good.rationale: Led the Screen Actors Guild and noted he was a lifetime AFL-CIO member, and named free trade unions as a core democratic value, yet fired striking air traffic controllers in 1981.

property-fundamental.rationale: In 1964 argued that private property rights had been diluted and that holding a title means little if government holds power over the property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Cut the growth of federal regulation, deregulated oil, trucking and rail, and listed cutting regulation as a pillar of his recovery program.

cut-welfare.rationale: Said programs should aim to reduce dependency, pressed to curb food stamps and AFDC growth, and spoke of breaking the 'bondage of dependency', while insisting the safety net for the truly needy stay intact.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Declared an all-out war on drug racketeers, signed the Anti-Drug Abuse Acts of 1986 and 1988 with tougher penalties.

state-harmful.rationale: Said government was 'the problem', yet insisted national defense was government's prime responsibility and supported a safety net.

limit-guns.rationale: Backed the Brady waiting-period bill in 1991 and said an AK-47 is not a sporting weapon, but signed the 1986 Firearm Owners Protection Act and said citizens may own guns for sport and home defense. As governor he signed the 1967 Mulford Act banning public carrying of loaded firearms.

empower-police-military.rationale: Built up the military and said defense is government's prime responsibility; pushed crime legislation, tougher sentences, and said the legal system overprotected criminals.

decide-locally.rationale: Vowed to restore the distinction between federal powers and those reserved to states and the people, and proposed a swap giving states AFDC and food stamps.

rehabilitation.rationale: Emphasized cracking down on career criminals and said the legal system overprotected criminals' rights.

traditional-family.rationale: Called faith, family, work and neighborhood the values restored in the 1980s and defended parental authority and traditional values.

abortion-legal.rationale: In his 1983 essay he called abortion on demand a threat to human life, criticized Roe v. Wade and backed efforts to reverse it; as governor in 1967 he signed the Therapeutic Abortion Act, which he later regretted.

more-religion-public.rationale: Told evangelicals that secularism had damaged the nation, urged prayer in schools and called an inaugural day of prayer.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Praised a 'new patriotism' and urged teaching children what America is and represents.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His 1986 law paired employer sanctions and tighter border control with legalization and kept legal immigration open; he called it preserving America's immigrant heritage.

free-trade.rationale: Told Congress that the benefits of free trade and the disasters of protectionism were clear, and said open trade is America's job-creating machine.

open-borders.rationale: In 1980 urged a better understanding with Mexico over fences and a work-permit approach, yet in 1986 emphasized regaining control of the borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Held growth to be the best way to reduce deficits and raise living standards.

revolution-justified.rationale: Framed the American patriots at Concord as rightly resisting and backed anti-communist insurgents, though he spoke of ballots over bullets for democracies.

central-planning.rationale: In 1964 mocked the claim that government planning could solve human misery and held that planning had failed after decades of trial.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Praised free trade, while his administration imposed Japanese car export quotas and motorcycle and semiconductor tariffs; mixed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Sought to dismantle the Energy Department and end subsidies to business, and argued government should not decide what the economy makes.

one-party-rule.rationale: Declared abhorrence of dictatorship in all forms, especially totalitarianism, and predicted Marxism-Leninism would end on the ash heap of history.

democracy-best.rationale: Called democracy a not-at-all-fragile flower and urged a campaign to promote it worldwide.

political-violence-never.rationale: Held that armed resistance to tyranny can be justified, citing Concord and supporting freedom fighters.

separate-church-state.rationale: Urged restoring the right to acknowledge God in classrooms, proposed a school-prayer amendment and argued religion belongs in public life.

military-superiority.rationale: Led a major military buildup and told the Soviets America would reduce its defenses only if the threat shrank.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Defended the profit motive against those who called it outmoded and rejected socialism as a solution.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Inferred: from his stated rejection of Marxism-Leninism and abhorrence of dictatorship in all its forms.

taxation-theft.rationale: Called high tax rates confiscatory and said rates of 90 percent robbed Americans, but he accepted taxation and signed tax-raising bills.

total-state.rationale: Called the Soviet doctrine of state supremacy over the individual the focus of evil.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said it was democracies that refused to use their nuclear monopoly for territorial or imperial gain and portrayed expansion as a Soviet trait.

school-vouchers.rationale: Called repeatedly for vouchers and tuition tax credits giving parents choice of school.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Campaigned against deficits and for a balanced budget, but the federal debt roughly tripled under his tax cuts and defence build-up; mixed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Tied liberty to free enterprise throughout his speeches and held that as government expands, liberty contracts.

national-self-determination.rationale: Said people worldwide hunger for self-determination and inalienable rights.

force-without-un.rationale: Ordered the 1983 invasion of Grenada and justified aid to insurgents as consistent with the OAS and UN charters rather than needing Security Council approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Said he believed in prayer and argued that faith-based values were the bedrock of the nation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Moved to remove 'all traces of unjust discrimination against women' from federal law and created a task force on legal equity for women.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Said civil rights progress must continue with no backsliding and condemned racism as having no place in the country.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Deregulated oil to move toward energy independence and his Interior Department opened federal lands to oil drilling and mining.

national-mission.rationale: Urged a global campaign to promote democracy and called freedom the universal right of all human beings.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Held defense to be government's prime responsibility, but kept Social Security, Medicare and a safety net for the needy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Called for opportunity 'with no barriers born of bigotry or discrimination' and said there is no room for racism or anti-Semitism.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Listed freedom of religious choice among the core values of the free world.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Described the American order as 'We the People' telling government what to do and supported free elections as a universal right.

vanguard-party.rationale: Inferred: from his stated rejection of Marxism-Leninism and one-party totalitarian rule.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Upheld the law banning strikes by government employees against the public safety and fired the controllers, but affirmed the right of private-sector workers to strike.

party-controls-media.rationale: Listed a free press among the values at the heart of American strength and condemned the Sandinistas for denying a free press.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Pursued strengthening of US alliances in Europe and Asia.

death-penalty.rationale: Asked Congress for crime legislation allowing use of the death penalty where necessary.

collective-defense.rationale: Stressed strengthening traditional alliances in Europe and Asia and worked with NATO allies on missile deployment.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Condemned the Sandinista persecution of the church and defended religious freedom.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Championed 'flatter rates' and signed the 1986 act collapsing brackets, but retained a graduated schedule rather than a single rate.

space-expansion.rationale: Directed NASA to build a permanently manned space station and called space the next frontier.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Listed freedom of religious choice among the core values of the free world.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Rejected closed markets as a disaster and pushed to knock down trade barriers abroad.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Urged teaching history built around America's own story and heroes rather than fashion.

patriotic-education.rationale: Said 'an informed patriotism is what we want' and urged schools to teach why the Pilgrims came and what the nation stands for.

delink-world-market.rationale: Argued that open trade and free markets lift nations and urged integration rather than withdrawal from the world economy.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Praised the Constitution as a document in which the people tell government what it may do.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Condemned totalitarianism as one political invention and listed the Gulag and Cambodia together with Auschwitz and Dachau.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: No recorded position found for his final view: he floated private Social Security accounts in 1964 but dropped the idea in office.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Supported the Contras and other 'freedom fighters' resisting Soviet-backed governments as the Reagan Doctrine.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Condemned the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan and suppression of Polish Solidarity.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: his administration ended the CETA public-service jobs program and held that growth, not state employment, creates jobs.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Fired controllers for striking in violation of their oath and the law, and quoted approvingly a controller asking how he could ask his kids to obey the law if he did not.

non-intervention.rationale: Sent troops to Grenada and backed insurgencies; rejected any bar on intervening against hostile regimes.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Condemned anti-Semitism and hate groups as having no place in America.

defeat-communism.rationale: Predicted Marxism-Leninism would be left on the ash heap of history and urged support for forces resisting Soviet-backed regimes.

religion-illusion.rationale: Presented faith and prayer as central to the nation and to his own life and criticized secularism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Credited the American economy's prosperity to unleashing individual energy and enterprise, and said markets were producing growth worldwide.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Held that free enterprise and freedom were the foundation of a good society and that communism was the 'focus of evil', leaving no room for a third course.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Named Auschwitz and Dachau among the inhumanities of totalitarianism in his Westminster address.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Condemned the suppression of Polish Solidarity and listed free elections and free unions as core values.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Expanded the armed forces and called defense government's prime duty.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Led the Western bloc against the Soviet Union and urged allies to hold firm.

racial-franchise.rationale: Signed the 1982 25-year extension of the Voting Rights Act after dropping a plan to ease it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Cast Soviet atheism and state supremacy over individuals as the evil he opposed.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Pointed to hundreds of thousands of private groups doing social work and said family and community offer the best chance of reducing dependency, while keeping federal safety-net programs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Framed the Cold War as a struggle between right and wrong, good and evil, and called the Soviet system the focus of evil.

independent-unions.rationale: Praised the Solidarity movement and named free trade unions among the values that underpin freedom.

person-over-state.rationale: Opposed the Soviet claim of the state's omnipotence over the individual and said 'We the People' tell government what to do.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Argued that faith in God underlies American values and that a materialist, godless state violates human nature.

arms-reduction.rationale: Sought the 'total elimination one day of nuclear weapons', proposed the zero option and signed the INF Treaty with intrusive verification.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Repeatedly urged a constitutional amendment mandating a balanced federal budget and a line-item veto.

farm-price-support.rationale: Said farmers are best helped by reform, lower interest rates and open foreign markets rather than expanding federal payments, and criticized the cost of price-support programs in 1964.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Opposed a nuclear freeze and unilateral disarmament while the Soviets held arms, pursuing modernization and the zero option.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Signed the 1986 Anti-Drug Abuse Act that set mandatory minimum drug penalties and urged tougher sentences and tighter parole.

notes: Born 1911, died 2004. He was a New Deal Democrat until the 1950s and switched to the Republican Party in 1962; answers use his positions as president and in the 1964 Goldwater speech. On abortion he signed California's 1967 Therapeutic Abortion Act as governor but from about 1980 on opposed abortion firmly, and the later position is used. His 1986 immigration law is read as a record of enforcement plus legalization. Where his rhetoric (low taxes, balanced budget) differed from his record (TEFRA and other tax rises, large deficits) the answer follows the stated position and says so. Few answers rely on inference; none was added to pass the salience check.
